A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, White-Box Sensitivity Auditing with Steering Vectors. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLM auditing experiments across four decision tasks, including perturbation comparisons, steering robustness tests, and Sobol sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Both versions use WMD steering vectors, activation interventions, regression-based sensitivity estimates, and invariance/dependence tests. V2 reorganizes extraction, intervention, and compliance into separate stages, but these procedures were already described in v1; no algorithmic change is established.

E1.justification: Both retain judicial, South German credit-scoring, admissions, and DiversityMedQA tasks. The concept-extraction corpora, alternative Racial Identity data, and name-based perturbation scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same explicit and implicit black-box perturbations, attribute-free controls, and alternative steering-vector comparisons. Comparator membership in Tables 2–7 is unchanged.

E3.justification: The model roster, splits, metrics, and sample sizes remain unchanged, including 500 judicial sentence pairs and 1,000 credit profiles. V2's expanded account of neutralizing inputs and selecting/scaling vectors restates procedures already reported in v1.

E4.justification: The alternative-vector robustness tests, name-perturbation validity experiment, Sobol analyses, and steering-coefficient curves are retained without new analyses. V2's explanation of the low-bias admissions and medical cases interprets existing evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report querying each judicial test instance five times and averaging outcomes. No repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 2–7 and all existing result plots retain their values and trends. For example, Table 3 keeps Llama3.1-8B's white-box and explicit-black-box credit-bias scores at -5.11 and -0.69, and Table 2 keeps Saul-7B's dialect-vector conviction sensitivity at 19.66. Changes to their interpretation do not introduce new results.

T1.justification: The linear-representation premise, Equations 1–3, invariance/dependence thresholds, and credit-risk orthogonality argument are unchanged. V2's dataset notation and expanded explanations clarify existing roles without adding formal results or changing mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain white-box sensitivity auditing, identifying dependencies missed by black-box tests, more consistent audits, and target-concept isolation. The 'reveals' to 'indicates' edits do not change their scientific scope, and the conclusion is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 replaces descriptions of 5% and 20% higher outcome probabilities with descriptions of sensitivity scores and potential internal dependencies. It also newly interprets low admissions/medical sensitivity as evidence against systematic over-reporting of bias. The limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 2.3 newly explains WMD's weighting by model-output probability disparities and its offset using neutral-prompt activations. These disclose details of the already adopted method rather than establish a procedural change. Code-access information and appendix task specifications remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is unchanged, but v2's contribution paragraph explicitly positions the audit as an adaptation of Kim et al. (2018) from post-hoc interpretability to systematic sensitivity testing. Section 2.3 also expands the rationale for choosing WMD over difference-in-means.

P1.justification: The central methodological exposition is substantially reorganized: v1 Sections 3.3–3.4 become three stages in v2 Sections 3.3–3.5, and the six-step framework is rewritten around a running credit-scoring example. Expanded extraction explanations and explicit connections between stages materially reshape the method narrative.

P2.justification: V2 adds a workflow schematic as Figure 1. Existing Figures 1–6 become Figures 2–7 with unchanged graphics, while tables and figures shift position as the text reflows. Existing display structures remain essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the auditing procedure easier to follow through clearer stages, additional WMD details, and a workflow diagram. Section 4.4 also reduces the earlier conflation of steering sensitivity with outcome-probability differences. These improve clarity and interpretive precision, while the empirical evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
